objective: Recognize amino-acid, peptide and protein structural foundations.
evidence_of_understanding: Given a simple biomolecular structure, identify the α-amino-acid framework, a peptide bond and whether the example represents an amino acid, peptide or protein.

objective: Relate protein structural levels to interactions and function.
evidence_of_understanding: Explain how primary sequence and covalent/noncovalent interactions support higher-order protein structure and a structure-function relationship.

objective: Analyze folding and denaturation using sequence and environment.
evidence_of_understanding: Compare a native and denaturing condition and predict which interactions or structural levels are most affected without assuming peptide-bond hydrolysis.

objective: Evaluate protein structure-function evidence and model limits.
evidence_of_understanding: Critique a protein function claim by separating direct structural evidence from folding-model assumptions and context dependence.

objective: Recognize monosaccharides, anomers and glycosidic bonds.
evidence_of_understanding: Identify a monosaccharide ring, the anomeric carbon, α/β anomerism and a glycosidic linkage in a simple structure.

objective: Relate glycosidic linkage to polysaccharide structure.
evidence_of_understanding: Compare two polysaccharides with different linkage position or stereochemistry and predict a structural consequence.

objective: Compare carbohydrate structure-function relationships.
evidence_of_understanding: Use linkage and polymer structure to explain a difference in storage, structural or recognition function.

objective: Evaluate carbohydrate claims without taking X04 food ownership.
evidence_of_understanding: Evaluate a carbohydrate claim while keeping biochemical structure-function evidence separate from food-system or nutrition ownership.

objective: Recognize fatty acids, storage lipids and phospholipids.
evidence_of_understanding: Distinguish a fatty acid, triacylglycerol and phospholipid from representative structures.

objective: Explain amphipathic lipid self-organization in water.
evidence_of_understanding: Use hydrophilic/hydrophobic regions to explain why phospholipids can form bilayer structures in water.

objective: Analyze composition effects on membrane organization.
evidence_of_understanding: Predict how chain length, unsaturation or temperature changes packing and membrane fluidity.

objective: Evaluate lipid structure-function evidence and boundary limits.
evidence_of_understanding: Critique a lipid-function claim and distinguish biochemical evidence from later materials or application ownership.

objective: Distinguish nucleotide, nucleoside, DNA and RNA foundations.
evidence_of_understanding: Identify base, sugar and phosphate components; distinguish nucleotide from nucleoside and state a basic chemical distinction between DNA and RNA.

objective: Explain directionality, complementarity and base pairing.
evidence_of_understanding: Annotate 5′→3′ directionality and complementary antiparallel pairing in a simple nucleic-acid representation.

objective: Analyze sequence-structure-function relationships in nucleic acids.
evidence_of_understanding: Explain how sequence and pairing/stacking can affect nucleic-acid structure and a functional role.

objective: Evaluate nucleic-acid evidence without taking later information-domain ownership.
evidence_of_understanding: Evaluate a nucleic-acid chemistry claim while keeping information-processing ownership outside C08.

objective: Explain enzyme catalysis and active-site specificity.
evidence_of_understanding: Explain how an active site can provide selective binding/catalytic conditions and why an enzyme changes rate rather than equilibrium.

objective: Interpret saturation and Michaelis-Menten assumptions.
evidence_of_understanding: Interpret a simple substrate-versus-rate curve and state that Michaelis-Menten saturation conclusions depend on model assumptions.

objective: Analyze inhibition and regulation using kinetic evidence.
evidence_of_understanding: Compare kinetic patterns under an inhibitor or regulatory change and relate the observation to a plausible mechanism without overclaiming.

objective: Evaluate enzyme models while preserving C07 kinetics ownership.
evidence_of_understanding: Critique an enzyme-kinetics model by separating C08 biochemical context from C07 general kinetics/thermodynamics theory.

objective: Distinguish catabolism, anabolism, ATP coupling and redox carriers.
evidence_of_understanding: Classify steps as catabolic/anabolic and identify ATP coupling plus an oxidized/reduced carrier pair in a simple pathway.

objective: Trace matter, energy and redox bookkeeping through a pathway.
evidence_of_understanding: Track a conserved atom set, ATP coupling and reducing-equivalent transfer through a simplified biochemical pathway.

objective: Analyze central metabolic modules and flux regulation.
evidence_of_understanding: Explain how a central pathway module connects to another and how enzyme activity, substrate availability, compartment or signal can alter flux.

objective: Evaluate metabolic-network claims without taking X03/X04/C10 ownership.
evidence_of_understanding: Evaluate a metabolic-network claim while keeping health, food and industrial/environmental application ownership outside C08.

objective: Define measurable biomolecular structure-function design goals.
evidence_of_understanding: Turn a qualitative biomolecular design goal into a measurable structure-function hypothesis and outcome metric.

objective: Distinguish affinity, specificity, activity and context.
evidence_of_understanding: Given binding/activity observations, distinguish affinity from specificity and explain why neither alone establishes efficacy or safety.

objective: Analyze perturbation, screening and directed-evolution evidence.
evidence_of_understanding: Compare rational perturbation, screening and directed-evolution evidence and identify confounding effects from folding, dynamics or expression.

objective: Evaluate design-build-test-learn claims with X03/X04 and C09-C10 boundary discipline.
evidence_of_understanding: Evaluate an iterative biomolecular-design claim while keeping health, food, materials and industrial/environmental applications as boundary contexts.
